QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_55

question.text: A portfolio manager holds Rs 500 crore in government bonds and wants to hedge interest rate risk using bond futures. The cheapest-to-deliver bond has a conversion factor of 0.92. If the bond portfolio's modified duration is 7.5 years and the CTD bond's modified duration is 6.8 years, approximately how many futures contracts (each with Rs 2 lakh face value) should be used for a duration-neutral hedge, using the stem's conversion-factor-adjusted formula?

answer.text: Approximately 29,971 contracts [Hedge ratio = (Portfolio value / Futures face value per contract) x (Portfolio duration / CTD duration) x (1 / Conversion factor) = (500,00,00,000 / 2,00,000) x (7.5 / 6.8) x (1 / 0.92) = 25,000 x 1.10294 x 1.08696 ≈ 29,971]
25,000 contracts (simply Rs 500 crore / Rs 2 lakh per contract, ignoring duration and conversion factor adjustments)
27,574 contracts (adjusting for duration but not for conversion factor)
20,000 contracts (using a standard 80% hedge ratio without duration or conversion factor adjustment)

explanation.text: The Logic: Number of contracts = (Portfolio value / Contract face value) x (Portfolio modified duration / CTD modified duration) x (1 / Conversion factor) = (500,00,00,000 / 2,00,000) x (7.5 / 6.8) x (1 / 0.92) = 25,000 x 1.10294 x 1.08696 ≈ 29,971 contracts. The Trap: Dividing portfolio value by contract face value alone (25,000) ignores both adjustments. Adjusting only for duration (27,574) ignores the conversion factor. A flat 80% rule (20,000) ignores both. Earlier published versions of this item rounded to ~29,891, which slightly misapplies the multiplication; the more accurate arithmetic gives ~29,971. Note: The workbook itself frames the duration-based hedge using portfolio modified duration, market value, futures modified duration, futures price (or PAR) and lot size; the conversion-factor adjustment used here is an additional refinement to align with the CTD-bond pricing convention. Dynamic re-balancing is needed as duration, CTD identity and conversion factors change.
